messages:
Anya (Product Design): dropped a few quick screenshots + a short writeup of the change I'm proposing for the compare view — trying to address clutter in the left filter rail and make pinning versions feel less like a toggle and more like 'pinned context'. figma: https://www.figma.com/file/abc123/compare-rail-ideas :eyes: Sam (PM): nice! can you call out the user problem quickly? who sees the pinning affordance today and why do we expect them to use it? Anya (Product Design): sure — TL;DR: power users have 6+ pinned versions across teams; surface noise from filters makes scanning harder; current pin is tiny & ambiguous, people treat it like a per-row 'sticky' but expect a global compare anchor. goal: make pinning conceptually a 'compare lane' so users know what stays fixed. Rachel (Design): love the 'lane' metaphor. first glance: the new rail collapse feels heavier. can we keep a thin collapsed state with just badges/counts? right now collapsed used full width and it's jarring when toggling. :thinking: Leo (Frontend): technically we already have a collapsed rail component we can reuse. downside: animating width cause layout shift on the table which hurts perceived performance. might need `position: absolute` overlay for the collapsed state. Kai (Eng): agreed with Leo. overlay approach avoids reflow but introduces stacking/context issues with tooltips and keyboard focus. we'll need to manage focus trap. Alex (A11y): focus trap + overlay is fine, but ensure keyboard users can open/close with Enter/Space and we expose `aria-expanded` on the rail toggle. also announce pinned lane change via `aria-live="polite"`. example snippet:```html
Filters collapsed
``` Anya (Product Design): good call — I'll update the spec. also thinking about copy: instead of a pin icon with tooltip 'pin', rename to 'Pin to compare' and on hover show short explanation: 'Keep this version in your compare lane'. less ambiguous. Sam (PM): +1 on clearer copy. Julie, any analytics that shows how often people pin vs just expand filters? Julie (Data): quick check — about 12% of compare sessions interact with the pin control, but only 4% keep more than 1 pinned after 30s. suggests discoverability is okay but retention is low. if we make pinned lane persistent across nav, retention should rise. i can instrument events for `pin.create`, `pin.remove`, `pin.persisted-session`. Leo (Frontend): fwiw, persist across nav means saving to localstorage or to the server? localstorage is fastest but misses cross-device. Sam (PM): product decision: start with localstorage, iterate to server-side for org accounts. Anya (Product Design): UX question — when a user pins multiple versions, do we show them as mini-tabs in the lane or as stacked chips? current mock shows chips, but chips compress poorly. Rachel (Design): mini-tabs might scale better visually for quick switching. chips are good for scanning counts/metadata though. maybe hybrid: tabs for active switching, chips inside an overflow menu for >4 pins. Alex (A11y): tabs have strong keyboard affordances by default. if we implement pseudo-tabs with buttons, make sure `role="tablist"` + `role="tab"` + `aria-selected` applied. Kai (Eng): note on implementation: tabs means changing focus patterns in the compare table — we need to ensure screen reader users moving between table and tabs isn't confusing. we'll prototype with `role=tablist`. Anya (Product Design): another bit: performance badges. current badges show 'p95 latency' and 'cost/token' inline. stakeholders want them visible in compact row but designers fear clutter. proposal: badges collapse to an icon-only summary with hover tooltip showing the metrics. Rachel (Design): icon-only with hover tooltip ok, but touch devices need an explicit tap-to-expand. consider making the chip tappable to open a lightweight flyout with metrics. Leo (Frontend): tooltips + flyouts are doable. performance wise, lazy-load metric numbers when the flyout opens to reduce payload. Julie (Data): metric data OK to lazy-load; we already expose a lightweight metrics endpoint filtered by model id. pulling on demand reduces main listing latency. Sam (PM): timeline — can we ship the collapsed rail + pin lane + icon-only badges in next sprint? Kai (Eng): needs ~2 weeks dev + 3 days QA. if we drop persistent server pinning that's separate. Anya (Product Design): I'll update the Figma with: 1) collapsed thin rail state, 2) lane/tab hybrid for pins, 3) icon-only performance badge pattern, 4) updated copy 'Pin to compare' and microcopy for touch. pinging @Leo and @Alex for dev/a11y review after I update. Rachel (Design): small microcopy nit — 'Pin to compare' vs 'Pin to Compare' (title case). prefer sentence case 'Pin to compare' for consistency across console. Alex (A11y): also recommend adding visible focus styles for pinned items; low-contrast outline can break WCAG, use 3:1 contrast for focus stroke. Leo (Frontend): noted. will add CSS token `--focus-stroke` and ensure it meets ratio. ci-bot: deploy scheduled: staging build 2026-04-01 06:00 UTC for UI experiments. :rocket: Sam (PM): thanks everyone — great, concise feedback. Anya, after you update figma, drop the link here and I'll add to the sprint backlog. :thumbsup:
